# package pushstore

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/server/pushstore"
```

Package pushstore persists the push certificate management of a server (OPC 10000-12 §7.10): the trust lists of its certificate groups, their certificates and private keys. A [Store](#type-store) is the PushManagement.Store of package server: it writes each ApplyChanges and ResetToServerDefaults in one atomic write and restores what it wrote when the server is created again.

It is built on package uafx/fxstore, the persistence of the library: a Store is one [fxstore.Domain](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/uafx/fxstore#Domain) (namespace "push") on an [fxstore.Store](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/uafx/fxstore#Store) backend, by default an [fxstore.FileStore](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/uafx/fxstore#FileStore) in a directory of its own ([OpenDir](#func-opendir)). Each write is one Domain.Apply with the next revision. A write with an unknown outcome fences the store: later writes are refused until Settle has found what the backend holds and, where the write landed although the server did not apply it, has written the state the server has back. A server therefore never restarts with changes it did not apply, and never with a part of an ApplyChanges.

The records, by key in the namespace:

	tl/<group>         the trust list of a group: a format byte (1), the
	                   LastUpdateTime (Unix nanoseconds, a signed varint
	                   of encoding/binary, 0 for none) and the
	                   TrustListDataType in the OPC UA Binary encoding
	                   (Part 6 §5.2).
	cert/<group>/<t>   the certificate of type t (the numeric NodeId of
	                   the CertificateType in namespace 0, decimal): a
	                   format byte (1), a kind byte (0: deleted, 1: a
	                   certificate) and, for a certificate, the DER
	                   certificate, the private key in PKCS #8 DER
	                   (unencrypted) and the DER issuers, each with a
	                   uint32 little-endian length; the issuers follow
	                   their uint32 count.

\<group> is the BrowseName of the group, path-escaped. A deleted certificate is kept as a record, so that a certificate of the configuration that DeleteCertificate removed stays removed after a restart. ResetToServerDefaults deletes every record: the server then starts with its configuration.

The private keys are stored unencrypted: a FileStore creates its directory 0700 and its files 0600, and refuses a directory the group or others may write. An application that needs encryption at rest wraps the fxstore.Store it passes to Open. A key that cannot be exported in PKCS #8 (a key in a hardware module) cannot be stored: the write fails and ApplyChanges with it.

## Functions

### func GroupName

```go
func GroupName(n *ua.NodeID) (string, error)
```

GroupName returns the BrowseName of the certificate group with the NodeId n: a null NodeId is the DefaultApplicationGroup (Part 12 §7.10.4), the NodeIds of ServerConfiguration name the default groups, and the String NodeId "CertificateGroups.\<Name>" a group of PushManagement.CertificateGroups, in any namespace.

### type Store

```go
	// Close closes backend

	// restore, when not nil, is the state the store must hold again: that
	// before a write with an unknown outcome, which the server did not
	// apply.

}
```

Store is the store of the push certificate management of one server. It implements server.CertificateBatchStore, server.CertificateLoadStore, server.CertificateGroupStore and server.CertificateDeleteStore. It is safe for concurrent use; its writes are serialized.

#### func Open

```go
func Open(ctx context.Context, s fxstore.Store, o Options) (*Store, error)
```

Open opens the store on the backend s, which holds nothing else: the namespace "push" must be the only one in it. It fails when s cannot be loaded, belongs to another owner, was written by a newer version, or holds a record that does not decode (fxstore.ErrCorrupt). Close does not close s.

#### func OpenDir

```go
func OpenDir(ctx context.Context, dir string, o Options) (*Store, error)
```

OpenDir opens the store in the directory dir with an fxstore.FileStore, creating it if missing. The directory belongs to the store: it holds the lock file and the data file of the FileStore and nothing else. Close closes the FileStore.

#### func (Store) Close

```go
func (s *Store) Close() error
```

Close closes the store, and the backend of OpenDir. Writes after Close fail with ErrClosed.

#### func (Store) LoadCertificates


LoadCertificates returns what the store holds, sorted by key.

#### func (Store) Settle

```go
func (s *Store) Settle(ctx context.Context) (bool, error)
```

Settle resolves a write with an unknown outcome: it establishes what the backend holds (fxstore.Domain.Settle) and, when the write landed, writes the state before it back. It returns true when the store accepts writes again. Every write settles first, so an application may leave Settle to the next ApplyChanges or run it with a backoff.

#### func (Store) Status

```go
func (s *Store) Status() fxstore.DomainStatus
```

Status returns the state of the domain of the store: its revision and whether it is fenced.

#### func (Store) StoreChanges

```go
func (s *Store) StoreChanges(ctx context.Context, c server.CertificateChanges) error
```

StoreChanges writes c in one atomic write: the trust lists and the certificates with their keys, and the deletions. With c.Reset it deletes every record instead.
